message.content:
Below is everything you’ll need to pull up‑to‑10 files that have communicated with **12.234.56.126** from VirusTotal V3.  
(If you’re still on the legacy “v2” endpoints let me know – I’ll show those too.)

---

### 1️⃣ Build the request URL  

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files
    ?limit=10          # maximum results per page
    &cursor=pointer   # your pagination token (if you already have one)
```

> *Tip:* If this is your first run you don’t need `cursor=`—just omit it.

---

### 2️⃣ Set the HTTP headers  

| Header            | Value |
|-------------------|-------|
| `Accept`          | `application/json` |
| `x-apikey`        | `my_api` |

*(VirusTotal uses the custom `x-apikey` header instead of the standard `Authorization`.)*

---

### 3️⃣ Example cURL command  

```bash
curl -s \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "x-apikey: my_api" \
"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10"
```

*Add `&cursor=pointer` at the end of the URL if you’re continuing a previous paginated result.*

---

### 4️⃣ Sample JSON response structure  

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e",
      "attributes": { ... },
      "relationships": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "total_results": 123,
      "page_number": 1,
      "per_page": 10,
      "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6IjEyMzQ1Njc4OTAiLCJhY3Rpb24iOiJyZXNvdXJlIn0="
    }
  }
}
```

Use the value under `"next_cursor"` if you wish to keep paging forward.

---

### 5️⃣ Quick Python helper (optional)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "my_api"
IP_ADDR = "12.234.56.126"

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDR}/files"
params = {"limit": 10}

headers = {
    "accept": "application/json",
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
print(resp.json())
```

Replace `params["cursor"] = "<your_pointer>"` when you continue.

---

#### Gotchas & Limits

| Issue | What to watch out for |
|------|------------------------|
| Rate limit | 4 requests/minute for free tier, higher for paid tiers. |
| Pagination | Each page returns up to 100 items (`maxResults`) – here capped at 10. |
| Data freshness | Results may lag behind real‑time traffic by ~30 seconds–a few minutes. |
| Privacy | Only public metadata is returned unless you’ve purchased the “Enterprise” plan. |

That’s all! Run the above against your own environment, swap in your actual API key, and you’ll see the list of files that hit that IP. Let me know if you’d like help parsing the JSON into something more readable or integrating it into another workflow.
